records.name: Availability
records.definition: The proportion of time a system is operational and able to serve requests.

records.name: Security

distinctFrom.reason: Security protects data and behavior from attack, while model safety prevents a model's harmful inputs, outputs and actions.
Security limits what can reach a system, while runtime extensibility opens it to new capability as it runs.
Security is one expectation of a system, while quality is how far it meets all of them.
Security is protection from misuse, while architecture compliance is conformance to the intended structure.

records.definition: The degree to which a system protects its data and behavior from unauthorized access, misuse, or attack.

records.name: Simplicity

distinctFrom.reason: Simplicity is the absence of unneeded structure, while locality of behavior keeps related behavior together even at the cost of some duplication.

records.definition: The absence of unnecessary structure, keeping a system easy to understand and change.

records.name: Debuggability

distinctFrom.reason: Debuggability is locating and understanding a fault, while traceability is following one request or change end to end.
Debuggability serves finding faults, while auditability serves accounting for sensitive actions.
Debuggability is how easily a fault is understood, while strong consistency is every read seeing the latest write.
Debuggability is understanding faults, while ordering is processing events in one defined sequence.

records.definition: The ease with which a fault can be located and understood from a system's observable behavior.

records.name: Maintainability

distinctFrom.reason: Maintainability is the ease of changing a system, while pattern consistency is one problem solved one way, which helps it.

records.definition: The ease with which a system can be corrected, adapted, and extended over its lifetime.

records.name: Complexity
records.definition: The degree of interdependence and intricacy that makes a system harder to reason about and change.

records.name: Fault Isolation
records.definition: The degree to which a failure in one component is contained and prevented from cascading to others.

records.name: Architecture Compliance
records.definition: The degree to which an implementation conforms to its intended architectural rules, boundaries, and constraints.

records.name: Coordination Overhead
records.definition: The additional cost incurred to synchronize and coordinate concurrent or distributed units of work.

records.name: Data Integrity
records.definition: The accuracy, consistency, and validity of data maintained over its entire lifecycle.

records.name: Discoverability

distinctFrom.reason: Discoverability is how easily anything in a system is found and understood, while glob resolvability is one pattern collecting a whole concern.

records.definition: The ease with which a system's components, capabilities, or endpoints can be found and understood.

records.name: Mapping Overhead
records.definition: The additional cost of translating data or calls between two differing representations or models.

records.name: Operational Overhead
records.definition: The ongoing effort and resource cost of deploying, running, and maintaining a system in production.

records.name: Ordering
records.definition: The guarantee that events or messages are processed in a well-defined, consistent sequence.

records.name: Partial Availability
records.definition: The condition in which a system continues serving a subset of its functions while some components are unavailable.

records.name: Performance
records.definition: The speed, throughput, and resource efficiency with which a system performs its work.

records.name: Policy Complexity
records.definition: The difficulty of understanding, maintaining, and reasoning about a policy as its rules multiply.

records.name: Readability
records.definition: The ease with which source code can be read and understood by a developer.

records.name: Reliability

distinctFrom.reason: Reliability is functions performing correctly over time, while data integrity is the data staying accurate and valid over its life.

records.definition: The degree to which a system performs its required functions correctly and consistently over time.

records.name: Resource Efficiency
records.definition: The degree to which a system accomplishes its work using minimal computational resources.

records.name: Retry Safety
records.definition: The property that an operation can be retried without producing duplicate or inconsistent effects.

records.name: Robustness
records.definition: The degree to which a system continues to operate correctly under invalid input, stress, or unexpected conditions.

records.name: Static Safety

distinctFrom.reason: Static safety catches errors before code runs, while the security and debugging cost is what generating code at runtime adds.

records.definition: The guarantee that whole classes of errors are caught at compile time, before code runs.

records.name: Substitutability
records.definition: The degree to which a component can be replaced by another honoring the same contract without breaking clients.

records.name: Team Autonomy

distinctFrom.reason: Team autonomy is teams deciding without coordination, while independent scaling is parts of the system growing separately.

records.definition: The degree to which a team can make and deliver decisions independently, without cross-team coordination.

records.name: Tooling Complexity
records.definition: The effort required to set up, learn, and maintain the tools a technique or approach depends on.

records.name: User Experience
records.definition: The overall quality of a user's interaction with a system, including responsiveness, clarity, and ease of use.
